trace.code: st_params->buffer_bytes = le32_to_cpu(params->buffer_bytes); st_params->period_bytes = le32_to_cpu(params->period_bytes);  // guest-controlled virtio-snd PCM_SET_PARAMS, NO cap and NO spec check
size = iov_size(elem->out_sg, elem->out_num) - msg_sz; ... buffer = g_malloc0(sizeof(VirtIOSoundPCMBuffer) + size);  // size is the guest transfer-descriptor length, unbounded by buffer_bytes
buffer->size = size; buffer->offset = 0;  // the queued per-transfer host allocation is proportional to the guest descriptor
if (le32_to_cpu(params->buffer_bytes) > MAX_BUFFER_MIB * MiB) return VIRTIO_SND_S_BAD_MSG;  // cap at 500 MiB
if (le32_to_cpu(params->buffer_bytes) % le32_to_cpu(params->period_bytes) != 0) return VIRTIO_SND_S_BAD_MSG;  // VIRTIO 5.14.6.6.3.2 spec check
size = MIN(stream->params.buffer_bytes, size);  // cap each transfer allocation to the (now capped) buffer_bytes

preconditions: A QEMU VM with the virtio-snd (virtio sound) device attached (hw/audio/virtio-snd.c), reachable by a malicious guest
The guest sends VIRTIO_SND_R_PCM_SET_PARAMS with an oversized buffer_bytes and then queues TX/RX transfer descriptors of a matching size
No other host-side limit (cgroups/memory cgroup) is assumed; QEMU itself performed no cap before the fix

evidence.vulnerable_version: QEMU master before 259b58e68e / 9a0f03f815 (unreleased as of 2026-11-13; affects all released QEMU with virtio-snd)
evidence.fixed_version: QEMU master (commits 259b58e68e + 9a0f03f815, 2026-11-10, work_item 3587); not yet in a tagged release
evidence.observed_result: The verbatim vulnerable set_pcm_params accepts buffer_bytes=0xffffffff (4 GiB) with no cap, and the verbatim tx_xfer allocation computes sizeof+4GiB via g_malloc0 — an unbounded host allocation (the harness reports HOST OOM rather than performing the multi-GiB allocation). The verbatim fixed code rejects the 4 GiB buffer_bytes at the 500 MiB cap (VIRTIO_SND_S_BAD_MSG) and, for an in-range stream, caps a 4 GiB transfer to the 8 MiB buffer_bytes (a bounded 8388640-byte allocation).

real_exploit.target: qemu/qemu hw/audio/virtio-snd.c @ 259b58e68e^ (the exact buffer-size validation the fix replaced; commit message: 'A faulty/malicious guest can try to exhaust host memory')
real_exploit.backend: the vulnerable/fixed buffer-size validation reproduced byte-for-byte from virtio-snd.c and driven against real glibc malloc (g_malloc0); QEMU device types stubbed since the full QEMU object graph is not linkable standalone
real_exploit.demonstrated: vulnerable virtio-snd stores a guest-controlled 4 GiB buffer_bytes and performs an unbounded g_malloc0(sizeof + 4 GiB) host allocation per transfer (memory exhaustion / host OOM); fixed code rejects it at the 500 MiB cap and bounds each transfer to buffer_bytes.
